display.title: Episode 497: Dama ben Nesina and the Precious Stone (Kibbud Av Va'em)
display.summary_short: After the Tishrei holidays 5752: keeping the simchah going, Shema with a yeshiva boy, the Gemara's story of Dama ben Nesina, who would not wake his father for a fortune, and a listener's riddle.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi looks back on the shofar of Elul, Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, Sukkos and the Hakafos, and tells Tzivos Hashem soldiers that a happy face is part of their uniform. After the Hakochainik march, a yeshiva boy leads the Shema. Story time is about kibbud av va'em, the mitzvah in the Ten Commandments whose reward is long life. The Gemara tells of Dama ben Nesina, a kind farmer who honored his father in every way. He finds a huge precious stone in his field and keeps it in a box whose only key lies under his father's pillow. Messengers of the Kohen Gadol come looking for exactly such a stone, but Dama will not wake his sleeping father even for a fortune, and they leave without it. The next year a completely red heifer, a parah adumah, is born on his farm, and the same messengers pay him what they had offered for the stone. If a non-Jew was rewarded so, how much more will we be. In the mailbox, a boy from Brooklyn asks to come on the show and sends a riddle. The show closes with tzedakah and Shabbos candle-lighting time.
display.lesson: Honor your parents even at great cost; Hashem sees it and repays it richly.

date.note: 'Right after' Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, Sukkos and Hakafos; candles 6:05 fits Friday 11 Oct 1991. Tuesdays 24 Sep and 1 Oct were Yom Tov, so no show.
